answer.rationale: Memory c2 confirms the low-cost primary vendor has historically delivered sharp unit-cost cuts, accurate invoicing, and a stable onboarding profile, which means switching primary is a credible lever against the 18% mandate. Memory c4 shows that renegotiating at renewal recovered real margin by benchmarking the incumbent, moving them on both price and payment terms. Rather than fully switch primary (which would touch the assembly line running at 94% with no buffer and elevate delivery risk against the primary objective), I will negotiate_terms with the incumbent as the renewal window is exactly the lever that worked before, and use c2's pricing reference as the external benchmark so finance's 18% reduction target is achievable on paper without a vendor transition. The 14-day deadline is binding; a deferred decision was tried in c5 but only when preserving budget flexibility mattered more than capturing the discount, which is not the case here.
